documents.title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V3.0: PETG-CF
Bambu PETG CF Safety Data Sheet SDS20260701G50
Bambu Lab Filament Hex Code Table: PETG-CF
Filament guide: printer, nozzle, AMS, build plate and glue compatibility

notes: Mechanical keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values; the registry has one key per scope, so the Z values (tensile 29 ± 4 MPa, elongation 4.7 ± 0.4 %, bending modulus 1560 ± 180 MPa, bending strength 48 ± 4 MPa, impact 10.7 ± 1.6 kJ/m²) are not stored. Density, melting, glass transition, Vicat and HDT are raw-material properties (ISO 1183, DSC, ISO 306, ISO 75) and sit under material.* / thermal.*, apart from the printed-specimen mechanical.* rows.

TDS facts with no registry key are not stored: Young's modulus (X-Y 2460 ± 230 MPa, Z 1340 ± 150 MPa), melt index (19.3 ± 2.4 g/10 min at 250 °C, 2.16 kg), crystallization temperature (N/A), saturated water absorption rate (0.30% at 25 °C, 55% RH), printing and storage humidity (< 20% RH, sealed with desiccant), bed surface preparation (glue), retraction length (0.8 - 1.4 mm) and speed (30 - 60 mm/s), max overhang angle (~ 70°), max bridging length (~ 30 mm), support (Turn on), spool material (ABS, temperature resistance 70 °C) and spool size (diameter 200 mm, height 67 mm), suggested annealing of prints (55 to 60 °C, 65 to 70 hours, as printed), odor, skin hazards, chemical stability, solubility, chemical resistance, flammability and combustion products rows. Not stored although a registry key exists (one row per key, scope and region, or a type the key does not hold): heat deflection temperature 74 °C at 0.45 MPa (thermal.heat_deflection_temp keeps the 1.8 MPa row) and chamber temperature 35 - 50 °C (see the thermal.chamber_temp note).
The TDS recommended chamber temperature (35 - 50 °C) is not written to thermal.chamber_temp: that key is a printer capability (number, template field chamber_temp_max), not a filament print setting.

SDS facts with no registry key are not stored: product name "Bambu PETG CF", model "G50-xx", CLP "Not classified", the section 8 carbon-fibre handling warning (gloves when loading/unloading, cutting or sanding), and "Not hazardous goods" for sea (IMDG), DOT, road (ADR/RID) and air (ICAO/IATA) transport. Its section 8 also reads "carbon fiber-reinforced filament （Glass fiber-reinforced filament)", a wording slip in the SDS. Its section 9 "No data available" for melting point and density does not override the TDS values.

Source disagreements kept for review: bed temperature (TDS 65 - 75 °C vs material-table wiki 60 - 80 ℃ on the Engineering, Smooth PEI and Textured PEI plates and 60 - 80 °C in its glue table); oven drying temperature (TDS 65 °C, drying wiki and PETG wiki 60 - 65 °C, material-table wiki 70 ℃). The product TDS values are kept.

Nozzle guidance: the store page says "Stainless Steel Nozzle NOT Recommended"; the store FAQ, the PETG wiki and the material-table wiki say a hardened steel nozzle is required. Which size comes first differs: the material-table wiki recommends the 0.4 mm hardened steel nozzle first for Bambu PETG-CF, the store FAQ (5.Nozzle Recommendation) recommends 0.6 mm to reduce clogging. The 0.4 mm high-flow nozzle is "Not Recommended"; "not recommended" is not "not compatible", so no relation is written for it.

Printer guidance: the material-table wiki allows an open-frame or enclosed printer and recommends an enclosed one for PETG-CF; the store FAQ says to avoid an open-frame printer for Z-axis strength. Only the compatible_with family relation is written; "recommended" has no relation among compatible_with / not_compatible_with / requires.

Build plate guidance: the TDS lists glue as the surface preparation and the material-table wiki recommends glue stick or liquid glue; this is a recommendation, not a stated requirement, so no requires relation is written. The Bambu Cool Plate / PLA Plate is "Not recommended" for PETG-CF (material-table wiki), not "not compatible", so no relation is written for it either.

Marketing prose proves no number: "Enhanced Strength and Stiffness", "Ready for Outdoor Use" ("enhanced resistance to heat and moisture"), "Improved Mechanical Properties & High Flexibility" and "surface finish is glossier than that of PLA-CF" are not stored as values.

Hex: all 6 store colours have exactly one hex cell, matched by the colour name without the code in parentheses. The table prints two codes with lower-case letters (#9f332a, #16b08e); they are stored upper-case for the published_hex CHECK, and each quote keeps the table's own spelling (the other four codes are digits only). The raw store value is "Titan Gray  (31101)" with two spaces; the package normalises it to "Titan Gray (31101)", which is the value_text used here.

The store page links a "Filament RoHS" certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/87dee4bc82c64829b94c0a8d6e55e23c.pdf) that was not cached and not read (skipped as a certificate), so safety.certifications is neither curated nor marked not_published.
The store page also links the wiki guide https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/general/swaping-new-filament-with-bambu-reusable-spool, which was not cached and not read.
material.diameter_tolerance (± 0.03 mm) is the store page's own row (Product Features › bullet 5); the TDS gives no tolerance, so it is not restated here and not marked not_published.
No in-the-box list: no official packing list exists for this filament (the store page has no What's in the Box section).

The store FAQ (4.Safety Tips) and the PETG wiki say the filament is not food-grade / not food-contact grade and warn of fine fibre debris; no registry key holds these. The PETG wiki gives a default flow ratio of 0.95 for Bambu PETG-CF; no registry key holds it.

Adjudication against the second extraction (50 field disagreements), each disputed fact re-read in the cached document it cites. Same fact, this file's form kept (29): the hex locators (row and column, confirmed by the table's layout), the store-page source_url on the AMS 2 Pro and AMS HT rows, the store-page witness for the AMS, AMS lite and 0.2 mm rows (the material-table and PETG wikis state the same facts and are named in the notes), the hardened-steel locator wording, the part target kind ("hotend" and "plate" are not target kinds, §B.2) and the plate target labels (the TDS Build Plate Type row's own words). Different values, this file's kept: material.type is the TDS p.3 Composition cell "PETG, carbon fiber", as in every other filament file, not the product name "PETG-CF" from the TDS title; thermal.heat_deflection_temp is the 1.8 MPa row (68 °C), as in every other filament file, the 0.45 MPa row (74 °C) being in its test_condition; material.spool_type stays the store bullet "Basic Reusable Spool" (unverified, scoped to "Filament with spool"), because the TDS row "Spool Material ABS (Temperature resistance 70 °C)" gives the spool's material, not its type. Added from the second extraction after checking the TDS p.1: extrusion.supported_nozzle_diameters (Nozzle Size 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm), as in the PLA-CF, PET-CF, ABS-GF and PA6-CF files; the compatible_with nozzle relation from the same row is kept beside it, as in those files. Not added: thermal.chamber_temp (TDS p.2 "Chamber Temperature 35 - 50 °C"; a printer key, see the chamber note; no filament file stores it). Kept although the second extraction lacked them, each stated by its document: the 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 mm nozzle relation (TDS p.1 Nozzle Size), the open-frame or enclosed printer relation (material-table wiki, 1. Printer) and the Refill requires spool relation (store FAQ, 3.Refill Guidelines). material.net_weight is written as 1 kg, the TDS's own figure (mergeCurated stores 1000 g with the text "1 kg").
